verdict: One real product bug (wrong inch-to-cm factor in the size chart) and one test bug; the other two failures point to an unstable local server on localhost:3100.

failures.test: Product extras › the size chart switches between inches and centimetres
failures.summary: The CM size chart uses a factor of about 2.45 instead of 2.54, so every centimetre value is about 3.5% too low.
failures.evidence: In inches row M is "M 39 27.5 8.5"; in CM it is "row \"M 95.6 67.4 20.8\"" (27.5×2.54=69.9, but 27.5×2.45=67.4; L 40.5→99.2 fits the same 2.45 factor). The CM toggle itself worked: heading "In cm" and "CM" [pressed].
failures.next_step: Fix the inch-to-cm conversion constant in the size chart component to 2.54 (it looks like 2.45, possibly a digit swap), then rerun this test.

failures.test: Product info › Add to Cart updates the header basket badge
failures.summary: Line 52 expects the Add to Cart button text to be "2", but the quantity is shown on the header badge, which updated correctly.
failures.evidence: locator('.product-info__add') received "Added" (8×) then "Add to Cart"; snapshot shows button "Basket, 2 items".
failures.next_step: Remove or retarget line 52 (the badge is already checked on line 53). Also move the "Added" check on line 54 before the badge check, because the button reverts to "Add to Cart" within the 10s timeout.

failures.test: Product info › shows the product name and price
failures.summary: The local server on localhost:3100 refused connections on both attempts, so beforeEach navigation failed before the test body ran.
failures.evidence: page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost:3100/ (167ms, page url chrome-error://chromewebdata/)
failures.next_step: Check the webServer/dev-server logs for a crash or restart during the run. Make sure Playwright's webServer config waits for port 3100 and keeps the server alive for all tests.

failures.test: Product extras › opening an accordion item reveals its content
failures.summary: Navigation timed out waiting for the load event on the first attempt and passed on retry; this is likely the same local server instability, not a product defect.
failures.evidence: TimeoutError: page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded (waiting until "load"); passed on attempt 2. The page had rendered with status 200, but "Delivery Date: Calculating delivery date" was still pending.
failures.next_step: Check whether the delivery-date request or another resource hangs and blocks the load event. Consider using waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' in gotoProduct, and look into server stability alongside the ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED failure.
